correctness.rationale: Exact superposed exponential event clocks give path weights q^n and conditional Gamma(n,1) durations. Next-to-minimal first-hit routes are counted by adding one opposite pair and removing precisely 2K premature visits to the target in each coordinate; geometric path-number bounds control all higher terms. A single crossing of Gamma density ratios gives the sharp total-variation coefficient. For the high-dimensional axial start, Bessel Green-function expansions have errors dominated by e^{-(1-2c)s} because c<1/2, establishing the uniform O(d^-2) remainder. The companion reproducible Python script passed 360 independent finite exact/comparison checks, which supplement the analytical proof.

originality.rationale: Hartmann–Majumdar explicitly compute the unmarked lattice first-passage/Green representation and show shortest final excursions numerically, so those facts are not new. The new mathematical information is the coordinate-labeled first-detour count and probability, the sharp Gamma total-variation constant for successful-segment durations, and quantified high-dimensional probabilities/mean hop corrections. Linn–Lawley already establish total-arrival-time and network geodesic laws, which do not give the conditioned marked-successful-path law. Complete relevant sections of both primary papers were inspected. Residual risk: the scalar aggregate coefficient is readily derivable from known Green functions, and some authors may regard the path refinements as implicit in classical renewal-counting methods; they are not claimed as a new general renewal mechanism.
residual_risks: The aggregate unmarked detour probability is an algebraic implication of existing exact scalar Green functions, and its presentation as a stand-alone novelty would be inappropriate; novelty is restricted to marked directions and sharp successful-duration error.
Classical conditioned-walk enumeration or a broader uninspected theorem may contain the directional and Gamma-TV results implicitly.

value.rationale: The motivating lattice paper explicitly investigates the final successful hop count, observes shortest-path localization in dimension and rate, and lacks a sharp quantitative explanation. The first nonminimal route occurs at a natural two-hop cutoff; its exact coordinate split quantifies how transverse detours dominate. The sharp Gamma-TV coefficient specifies when final-segment-duration approximations are reliable. At the same dimension-proportional rate discussed in the source, explicit 5/(8d) and 5/(4d) coefficients convert the observed high-dimensional approach into a checkable prediction. These natural path/geometric statistics do not rest on arbitrary parameter slicing or unsupported downstream claims.
